column5: Annoying, troublesome, persistent, or inconvenient, usually in a relatively light or playful way.
column6: annoying, bothersome, troublesome, irritating, pesky little
column7: I finally fixed that pesky formatting bug. / Mosquitoes are especially pesky around sunset. / One pesky little detail keeps ruining the whole plan.
column8: Usually lighter/cuter than infuriating or obnoxious. Common with small recurring problems, insects, details, errors, chores, etc. Can sound playfully minimizing.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0116, voca_0118, voca_0120 | search: pesky meaning

column5: An animation or visual-effects technique in which artists trace over or isolate elements from live-action footage frame by frame.
column7: The film used rotoscoping to give the animated movement a realistic quality.
column8: Raw search 'lotoscoping' normalized to rotoscoping. Modern VFX also uses rotoscoping to create masks/mattes around moving subjects.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0111, voca_0112 | search: lotoscoping

column5: I'm enjoying it, connecting with it, feeling comfortable with it, or responding positively to its mood/style/energy.
column6: I'm into it, I like the vibe, it's clicking with me, I'm feeling it
column7: I wasn't sure about the new art style at first, but now I'm vibing with it. / This playlist is exactly what I needed—I'm vibing with it.
column8: Modern casual slang. 'Vibe with' can mean like/get along with a person or resonate with an idea/style. Very register-sensitive.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0120 | search: i'm vibing with it meaning

column5: If an earlier invitation, proposal, promise, or opportunity is still available and has not been withdrawn or expired.
column6: if the offer is still open, if that's still available
column7: If the offer still stands, I'd love to come with you this weekend. / I know it's been a month, but if your offer still stands, I could use that help.
column8: An offer 'stands' when it remains valid/in force. Natural polite way to return to an earlier invitation after some time.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0118 | search: if the offer still stands meaning

column5: The otaku named or identified in a work's title; titular modifies the title-linked role, not necessarily 'main' by itself.
column7: The titular otaku is introduced before the rest of the cast.
column8: Contextual application of titular. Keep because the original search likely tested what titular means when attached to a role/category such as otaku.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0112 | search: titular otaku meaning

column5: Mercy or leniency shown by a person or authority toward someone subject to punishment, especially reduction, commutation, pardon, or relief from a sentence.
column7: The prisoner petitioned the governor for clemency. / The campaign asked for clemency rather than claiming the conviction never happened.
column8: Umbrella concept; exact mechanisms differ by legal system. A pardon, commutation, or reprieve may be forms of executive clemency, but they are not interchangeable.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0121 | search: clemency definition

column5: To repeatedly raise a false or exaggerated alarm, causing people to stop believing you when a real danger/problem occurs.
column6: raise false alarms, sound a false alarm
column7: If you keep crying wolf, people won't believe you when something serious actually happens. / He cried wolf so many times that nobody reacted to the real emergency.
column8: From Aesop's 'The Boy Who Cried Wolf.' The idiom focuses on loss of credibility through false alarms.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0119 | search: If you keep crying wolf, people won’t believe you when something serious actually happens.

column5: Depending on context, 'original character'—a character created by a fan/artist rather than belonging to an existing canon—or 'original content'—material created by the poster rather than reposted.
column7: She drew her OC interacting with characters from the series. / The post was tagged OC to show that the photographer had taken the picture themself.
column8: Very context-dependent. Fandom/art spaces strongly favor original character; Reddit/social platforms often use OC = original content. Other fields have many unrelated expansions.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0116 | search: oc meaning

column5: To begin eating eagerly; to prepare to resist or defend a position; or to settle in for sustained effort.
column6: tuck in, entrench oneself, get stuck in
column7: Dinner's ready—dig in. / The two sides dug in and refused to compromise.
column8: Several senses share the image of getting deeply engaged or entrenched. Context determines whether it means eat, resist, or work with determination.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0110 | search: dig in meaning
column12: entry::phrasal_verb usage::debate-friendly topic::planning topic::debate discovery::resolution discovery::debate_language

column5: Help yourself freely; take, eat, drink, use, or enjoy as much as you want or can.
column6: help yourself, have at it, go for it, knock yourself out
column7: There are plenty of leftovers in the fridge—fill your boots. / If you want to spend three hours reading every review before buying it, fill your boots.
column8: Often permissive, jocular, or slightly dismissive: 'If that's what you want, go ahead.' Literal boot-filling is not normally intended.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0113 | search: fill your boots

column5: A malignant cancer arising from epithelial cells—the cells that line or cover body surfaces, organs, and glands.
column7: The pathology report identified the tumor as a carcinoma. / Many common cancers are carcinomas, but not every cancer is a carcinoma.
column8: Medical lexical card only. Carcinoma is a category of cancer; contrast sarcoma (connective/supporting tissues), lymphoma, leukemia, etc. Diagnosis/subtype depends on pathology.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0121 | search: carcinoma

column5: In a religious manner; figuratively, with very regular, conscientious, or devoted consistency.
column7: She checks the forecast religiously every morning.
column8: Figurative religiously does not simply mean enthusiastically. It emphasizes faithful regularity or strict consistency, though enthusiasm may accompany it.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0111 | search: not religiously meaning not enthusiastically?

column5: A person who repeatedly causes someone pain, distress, fear, harassment, or suffering.
column7: Years later, he confronted one of his childhood tormentors. / The cat finally escaped its tiny tormentor—the neighbor's overexcited puppy.
column8: From torment. Can be serious (abuse/persecution) or exaggerated/playful depending on context.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0117 | search: tormentor

column5: A question asking how much progress someone has made on a task, book, project, process, etc. Natural in many varieties, though 'How far along are you with...?' is often more idiomatic in AmE.
column6: How far along are you?, how much have you done?, where are you with...?
column7: How far are you with the report? / How far along are you with the new deck? / How far are you in the book?
column8: Preposition depends on object: with a project/task; in/into a book, show, route; along with a process/project. Preserve search as natural but note AmE preference.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0121 | search: how far are you with meaning

column5: Extremely bitter, cruel, angry, or hateful criticism or language directed at someone or something.
column7: The actor was shocked by the vitriol directed at her online. / You can criticize the policy without pouring vitriol on everyone who supports it.
column8: Originally a chemical term associated with sulfuric acid/metal sulfates; modern figurative sense evokes corrosive language. Stronger than criticism or anger: vitriol suggests poisonous hostility.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0116 | search: define vitriol

column5: A style of rhythmic spoken music; a sharp knock; informal criticism/blame or a criminal charge; as a verb, to perform rap music, knock, or criticize/talk sharply depending on context.
column6: hip-hop vocal style; knock; blame, charge
column7: She started rapping over the beat. / There was a rap at the door. / He took the rap for a mistake the whole team made.
column8: Highly polysemous. Useful phrases: take the rap = accept blame/punishment; beat the rap = escape conviction (WID5849); bad rap = unfairly bad reputation. 'Rap sheet' = criminal record.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0114 | search: rap meaning
column12: entry::word usage::informal usage::conversational topic::music topic::crime discovery::criticism

column2: barf me out / barf someone out
column5: To disgust or gross someone out; 'barf me out' can function as an emphatic reaction meaning roughly 'that disgusts me / gross me out.' Separately, literal constructions with barf ... out can describe vomiting or ejecting something, depending on context.
column6: gross someone out, disgust, revolt, nauseate; make someone want to puke
column7: That totally barfs me out—it's disgusting. / Ugh, barf me out! / Literal/contextual: The creature swallowed him and then barfed him back out.
column8: KEEP + FIX. 'Barf someone out' is attested slang associated especially with 1980s Valley Girl/Valspeak-style speech, meaning 'disgust/gross someone out.' Modern speakers are more likely to say 'gross me out'; literal barf ... out is also compositionally understandable.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0117 | search: barf me out meaning

column5: A fence topped with or made from razor wire—security wire fitted with sharp blades/barbs designed to deter crossing.
column6: security fence, razor-wire barrier, concertina-wire fence (not always identical)
column7: The compound was surrounded by a tall razor-wire fence.
column8: Razor wire is a high-security barrier material. Concertina wire describes coiled wire form and may be barbed or razor-type; terms overlap in casual use but aren't exact synonyms.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0120 | search: razor wire fence

column5: A mocking or playful way to tell someone to leave the online world, reconnect with ordinary reality, and gain perspective.
column6: go outside, get offline, get some perspective, log off
column7: You've been arguing with strangers about fictional power levels for six hours—go touch grass. / I realized I was getting way too invested in the discourse and needed to touch grass.
column8: Usually teasing or dismissive; can be genuinely hostile. Literal image = go outdoors and physically reconnect with the real world. Often aimed at someone perceived as terminally online.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0114 | search: touch grass
column12: entry::slang_expression entry::phrase usage::slang usage::internet_slang usage::playful usage::informal topic::internet

column2: lost to time vs lost in time
column5: Lost to time means forgotten, destroyed, or no longer recoverable because time passed. Lost in time means stranded/displaced in another time, or figuratively absorbed/disconnected from the present.
column6: forgotten by history vs temporally stranded/absorbed
column7: The original ending is lost to time; no complete copy survives. / The time traveler is lost in time with no way home. / Walking through the old village, I felt almost lost in time.
column8: Preposition changes the image: TO time = time is what took/erased it; IN time = located or trapped within time. 'Lost in the mists of time' is another phrase for something historically obscure.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0114 | search: lost to time vs lost in time
column12: entry::contrast_set entry::phrase topic::history topic::language_learning discovery::contrast discovery::figurative_extension

column5: The state of being fashionable, popular, or widely accepted at a particular time.
column7: Minimalist interiors came into vogue again.
column8: Common patterns: be in vogue; come into vogue. Also the name of the fashion magazine, distinguished by context.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0110 | search: define vogue

column5: Noun: a long narrow channel beside land/roads for drainage. Verb: abandon, discard, leave, skip, or get rid of someone/something; also make an emergency landing on water.
column6: channel, drain; abandon, dump, skip, get rid of
column7: The car slid into a roadside ditch. / We ditched the original plan and started over. / He ditched class to go to the beach.
column8: Very productive informal verb: ditch a plan, date, class, friend. Aviation 'ditch' = intentionally land an aircraft on water in an emergency.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0120 | search: define ditch

column5: Lacking energy, enthusiasm, or interest; sluggish and unmotivated.
column7: He felt listless all afternoon and couldn't focus on anything.
column8: Related noun: listlessness. The 'list' here is an old word for desire or inclination, not a written list.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0110, voca_0111 | search: listless meaning

column5: The process of teaching beliefs or ideology so that they are accepted uncritically, especially while discouraging questioning or alternative views.
column7: The documentary examines allegations of political indoctrination in the school system. / Whether something counts as education or indoctrination often depends on how much room there is for evidence, disagreement, and questioning.
column8: Noun of indoctrinate. Strongly evaluative: calling education 'indoctrination' alleges a method or power relationship, not merely that values are being taught.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0114 | search: indoctrination meaning

column5: Relating to the systematic study and description of people, cultures, and social practices, especially through close observation and fieldwork.
column7: The researchers conducted ethnographic interviews in the community.
column8: Related noun ethnography; common in anthropology, sociology, design research, and qualitative research.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0111 | search: define ethnographic

column5: To take a risk and proceed despite uncertainty about the outcome or possible trouble.
column6: risk it, take a chance, gamble
column7: The forecast looked bad, but we chanced it and went hiking anyway. / I wouldn't chance driving that far on an empty tank.
column8: Usually 'chance it' or 'chance doing something.' Chancing = taking a risk. Different from 'by chance' = accidentally.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0121 | search: chancing meaning

column5: To have absolutely no knowledge or understanding of something.
column6: have no clue, have no idea, not have the foggiest, be completely in the dark
column7: I didn't have the faintest idea where he had gone. / I haven't the slightest idea why that button stopped working. / She had no idea—literally not the faintest clue—what they were referring to.
column8: Slightest and faintest intensify the negative: not even the smallest trace of an idea. Common patterns: 'I don't have the slightest/faintest idea,' 'I haven't the faintest,' and 'not the slightest clue.' 'Faintest' can sound slightly more idiomatic/BrE-flavored in the elliptical form.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0110 | search: I didn't have the slightest/faintest idea

column5: A shocking or highly surprising piece of news/revelation; also, dated/informal, a very attractive glamorous woman ('blonde bombshell').
column7: The documentary drops a bombshell halfway through: the witness had known him for years. / Her resignation was a complete bombshell. / 'Blonde bombshell' is an older glamour stereotype.
column8: Common: drop a bombshell, bombshell revelation/report. Figurative news sense is very common. Person sense can sound dated/objectifying.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0114 | search: bombshell meaning

column5: A 19th-century American philosophical and literary movement associated especially with Ralph Waldo Emerson and Henry David Thoreau, emphasizing intuition, individual conscience/self-reliance, nature, and spiritual reality beyond purely empirical/material experience.
column7: Emerson and Thoreau are central figures in American Transcendentalism. / The movement treated nature as a source of spiritual and moral insight.
column8: Existing cards cover Transcendentalist (person/adjective); this preserves the movement itself, which is distinct. Do not confuse broadly with Kant's technical use of 'transcendental.'
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0121 | search: transcendentalism definition

column5: Very energetic, intense, exciting, or powerful.
column7: It is a high-octane action movie from start to finish.
column8: Literally refers to fuel with a high octane rating; figuratively suggests power, speed, and intensity.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0110 | search: high octane meaning

column5: Archaic third-person singular present form of do: 'does.' Used with he/she/it or a singular subject in Early Modern English and modern imitation of archaic/biblical speech.
column7: 'The lady doth protest too much' uses doth where modern English would use does. / Fantasy dialogue sometimes throws in doth simply to sound old-fashioned.
column8: Pronounced roughly 'duth.' Do not combine modern -s with it: 'he doth know,' not 'he doth knows.' Modern parody often overuses doth for mock-Shakespearean flavor.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0117 | search: doth meaning
column12: entry::word usage::dated usage::archaic usage::religious topic::public_speaking topic::religion discovery::religious_origin

column5: In clinical neuropsychology, the production of false or distorted memories without conscious intent to deceive; more broadly/older, conversation or fabrication depending on context.
column7: A patient may confidently report an event that never happened because of confabulation, not deliberate lying. / In AI discussion, the word is sometimes borrowed metaphorically for invented outputs.
column8: Clinical confabulation is not simply lying: the person is not necessarily consciously deceiving. In AI, 'hallucination' is more established terminology, though both are metaphors.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0119 | search: confabulation meaning
column12: entry::word usage::specialist topic::communication topic::medicine topic::health discovery::specialist_knowledge discovery::specialist_register

column5: To give in, surrender, or abandon one's position under pressure from someone or something; in poker, to fold rather than continue against an opponent.
column6: give in to, cave to, yield to, surrender to, back down against
column7: He talked tough online but folded the moment his boss pushed back. / I wasn't going to fold to peer pressure. / In poker, she folded to his large raise.
column8: General slang is an extension of poker/card-game fold = withdraw from the hand. 'Fold under pressure' is more established; 'fold to X' is common in gaming/internet speech but can sound informal.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0116 | search: fold to someone meaning

column5: Directly opposing, competing, or fighting someone in a determined, evenly matched way.
column7: The smaller company is willing to go toe-to-toe with the industry leader.
column8: Raw search 'toe by toe' is most likely a misremembering of toe-to-toe.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0110 | search: toe by toe meaning

column5: The ease with which an asset can be converted into cash without greatly affecting its price; also the availability of cash or readily tradable assets.
column7: The company kept extra cash to maintain liquidity during the downturn.
column8: In markets, high liquidity also implies assets can be bought/sold readily with relatively low transaction impact.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0112 | search: liquidity meaning

column5: To collect information, material, or items from multiple sources and organize them into a list, book, report, dataset, etc.; in computing, to translate source code into another form that can be executed or processed.
column6: collect, assemble, gather, collate; build/translate code
column7: I compiled the bookmark searches into one candidate list. / The editor compiled the essays into a single volume. / The program won't run because the code fails to compile.
column8: Two major senses: assemble information; computing translation/build process. A compiler performs the latter. 'Compile a list/report/data' is very common outside programming.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0117 | search: define compile

column5: Extra stress or prominence placed on a word to contrast it with another possibility, correct an assumption, or highlight a particular distinction.
column6: contrastive emphasis, emphatic stress, corrective stress
column7: I said the BLUE one, not the green one. / 'SHE borrowed it' contrasts the borrower with someone else.
column8: Raw 'contrasive' repaired. Often realized through a combination of pitch accent, duration, intensity, etc., not just loudness. Closely related to contrastive focus.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0120 | search: contrasive stress

column5: To place or present oneself as comparable to, aligned with, or on a similar level to someone or something.
column6: compare oneself with, align oneself with
column7: He was reluctant to put himself alongside writers he had admired since childhood.
column8: Not a fixed idiom in every context; the metaphorical sense comes from placing two people or things side by side for comparison or alignment.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0110 | search: put oneself alongside someone else meaning

column5: Small clues, hints, details, or unanswered questions deliberately scattered through a story so the audience can gradually follow a mystery toward later revelations.
column6: clues, hints, planted details, trail of clues, narrative breadcrumbs
column7: The first episode drops mystery breadcrumbs about the brother's past without explaining them. / Good mystery breadcrumbs feel meaningful in retrospect rather than like random trivia.
column8: Creative extension of breadcrumb trail/Hansel-and-Gretel metaphor. In storytelling, breadcrumbs guide audience inference. Distinguish from web-navigation breadcrumbs and dating 'breadcrumbing.'
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0117 | search: mystery breadcrumbs

column4: phrasal verb, chiefly in fixed phrase
column5: To summon or gather an inner quality, especially courage; most common as 'pluck up the courage.'
column7: I finally plucked up the courage to ask. / She plucked up enough nerve to call him back.
column8: Most natural modern use is 'pluck up the courage.' Bare 'pluck up' without an object is uncommon. BrE flavor; 'muster the courage' is broadly natural.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0121 | search: pluck up definition

column5: A concise pitch letter sent to a literary agent or publisher to interest them in a book/manuscript, typically including the premise, key story information, author details, and requested materials according to submission guidelines.
column7: She revised her query letter before contacting literary agents. / A strong query should hook the agent without summarizing every scene.
column8: Publishing-specific. Requirements vary by agent/market; a query letter is not the manuscript itself and differs from a synopsis.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0120 | search: query letter meaning

column2: So, that is 2 p.m. on a Tuesday.
column3: /soʊ ðæt ɪz ˌtuː piːˈem ɑːn ə ˈtuːzdeɪ/
column5: A sentence that converts or restates prior information into a concrete time, often emphasizing how ordinary, inconvenient, or contextually significant that time is.
column6: in other words, that works out to, so that's
column7: The livestream starts at 19:00 UTC—so, that is 2 p.m. on a Tuesday for me.
column8: Preserve exact search because likely source/context mattered. 'On a Tuesday' can mean a typical/unspecified Tuesday or emphasize weekday context; for a specific date, 'on Tuesday' is usually enough.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0121 | search: so, that is 2 p.m. on a Tuesday meaning

column5: A deliberately comic or insulting phrase combining vile ('disgusting, morally repulsive, extremely unpleasant') with booty ('buttocks' in slang, or loot/treasure in another sense). Exact joke depends on source context.
column6: disgusting butt, awful booty; nasty loot (contextual)
column7: The line 'vile booty' sounds like exaggerated comic disgust if booty means someone's butt. / In a pirate joke, it could instead play on booty meaning stolen treasure.
column8: Not a fixed idiom. Preserve the exact wording because the humor likely comes from the collision of dramatic 'vile' with slangy 'booty,' and possibly from booty’s double meaning.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0116 | search: vile booty

column5: Pregnant is the neutral standard adjective. Alternatives vary strongly by register: expecting / expecting a baby (gentle/common), with child (old-fashioned/literary), carrying a baby (descriptive), knocked up (very informal, can be crude), up the duff (BrE slang), in the family way (old-fashioned euphemism).
column6: expecting, expecting a baby, with child, carrying a baby, knocked up, up the duff, in the family way
column7: She's pregnant. / They're expecting their first child in June. / 'Knocked up' may sound joking or disrespectful depending on speaker/context. / 'With child' sounds deliberately old-fashioned today.
column8: No synonym is perfectly interchangeable because register matters. 'Pregnant' is usually the safest neutral word. Existing 'knocked up' card covers one informal expression; this card maps the broader register spectrum prompted by the synonym search.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0117 | search: pregnant synonym

column5: To violently rob a place, especially during war or conquest; figuratively, to exploit or strip something of valuable resources or ideas.
column7: The invading army pillaged the town. / The studio was accused of pillaging its old catalog for recognizable ideas instead of developing new ones.
column8: Pillage/plunder often imply large-scale violent looting. Loot can be verb/noun and is broader. Figurative pillage is vivid and critical: pillage resources, archives, intellectual property, the past.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0114 | search: pillaging meaning
column12: entry::word usage::figurative usage::critical usage::military discovery::resource_allocation discovery::figurative_extension

column5: As a noun, an annoying, inconsiderate, or unpleasant person. As a verb, to move or pull suddenly and sharply, or cause something to do so. Also has other technical/slang senses.
column6: asshole (stronger/vulgar), idiot (not exact); yank, twitch, jolt
column7: Don't be a jerk—just tell her the truth. / The bus jerked forward and everyone grabbed the rail. / He jerked the door open when he heard the noise.
column8: Person-insult sense is common and moderately rude. Motion sense = sudden sharp movement. 'Jerk off' is separate vulgar sexual phrasal verb; physics 'jerk' = rate of change of acceleration. Context is crucial.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0115 | search: jerk meaning

column5: Self-important and excessively grand, formal, or dignified in a way that feels affected or ridiculous.
column7: He gave a pompous speech about how nobody else understood real cinema. / The phrase is grammatically fine, but it sounds a little pompous for a casual text.
column8: Pompous usually criticizes inflated self-importance. Pretentious emphasizes trying to seem more cultured/important than one is; grandiose emphasizes extravagant scale/style; stuffy emphasizes excessive formality/conservatism.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0114, voca_0115 | search: pompous

column5: A device that cools air by evaporating water; Japanese 冷風機 may also refer more loosely to a portable air cooler, so the best English term depends on the mechanism/product.
column6: swamp cooler (informal AmE), air cooler, portable air cooler
column7: An evaporative cooler works best in relatively dry air. / If the Japanese product is simply marketed as 冷風機 without true evaporative cooling, 'portable air cooler' may be safer.
column8: Do not automatically translate 冷風機 as air conditioner: many units do not use refrigeration/compressors and cool much less than AC. 'Swamp cooler' is common informal AmE for evaporative cooler.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0119 | search: 冷風機 英語で

column5: A complete or conspicuous failure, especially a movie, show, product, event, joke, or performance; as a verb, to fail badly. Also literally, to fall/drop loosely or heavily.
column6: failure, bomb, dud, fiasco; fail, bomb
column7: The movie was a box-office flop. / His first product launch flopped, but the second did well. / I flopped onto the couch after dinner.
column8: Entertainment/business sense is very common. Contrast 'flip-flop' and 'flop' physical movement. Online, people may call media a flop based on sales, reception, or simply as an insult.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0119 | search: define flop

column5: A small but prominent constellation in the southern sky, commonly called the Southern Cross.
column7: Crux is one of the best-known constellations of the Southern Hemisphere. / Its stars have long been useful for orientation in the southern sky.
column8: Distinct from ordinary crux = central/decisive point. Crux is Latin for cross. It appears on several national flags.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0119 | search: what is crux constellation

column5: Giving someone intermittent small signs of romantic interest or attention—messages, likes, vague plans—enough to keep them engaged without committing to a real relationship or meaningful progress.
column6: stringing someone along, leading someone on, giving mixed signals (broader), keeping someone on the hook
column7: He sends a flirty message every few weeks but never agrees to meet; it feels like breadcrumbing. / Breadcrumbing can keep someone emotionally invested through tiny bursts of attention.
column8: Metaphor of leaving a trail of breadcrumbs. Often discussed in dating, but can extend to employers/brands offering tiny hints/promises. Ghosting = abruptly disappearing; breadcrumbing = intermittent contact that sustains hope.
column10: voca_0110–0121 | folders: voca_0115, voca_0121 | search: breadcrumbing meaning
